summary: The Athletic ranks the home-field atmospheres of the eight remaining 2023 M.L.B. playoff teams after the Wild Card round showed how much crowds differ, with loud Target Field helping the Twins and sparse crowds at Tropicana Field sinking the Rays. Each entry gives venue facts, a memorable postseason moment and a take. The Phillies' Citizens Bank Park lands at No. 1 and the Diamondbacks' Chase Field at No. 8.
one_line: The Athletic ranks the eight remaining 2023 MLB playoff teams' home ballparks by how daunting they are, with Philadelphia's Citizens Bank Park first.
key_facts: The Twins used crowd noise at Target Field to pick off Vladimir Guerrero Jr. in Game 2 and complete a two-game Wild Card sweep of the Blue Jays; Carlos Correa realized the Jays' third-base coach couldn't be heard.
The Rays were swept by a Rangers team with nine fewer regular-season wins, playing before two of the smallest postseason crowds in the past 100 years.
Ranking from No. 8 to No. 1: Diamondbacks, Rangers, Twins, Astros, Braves, Orioles, Dodgers, Phillies.
Chase Field (opened 1998, capacity 48,405) drew 24,212 per game in 2023; the writers worry Dodgers fans, less than a seven-hour drive away, could fill the stands in the division series.

Globe Life Field (opened 2020) hosted 16 postseason games in 2020, all with the Dodgers, and the 2023 Rangers series was the first playoff baseball there with the Rangers; the Rangers averaged 31,272 in 2023.
The Twins snapped an 18-game postseason losing streak with two homers from rookie Royce Lewis, their first playoff win since Oct. 5, 2004, and won their first postseason series since 2002.
Minute Maid Park sold out 23 times and drew 3 million fans in 2023, but the Astros went 6-17 in those sellouts and 39-42 at home overall.

Truist Park had 54 sellouts and drew just over 3.19 million, the Braves' highest total since it opened in 2017; Atlanta has won six straight division titles and reached the playoffs 22 times since 1991.
Oriole Park at Camden Yards attendance rose by more than a half million from 2022, and the Orioles had the second-most wins in baseball in 2023.
Dodger Stadium (opened 1962, capacity 56,000) averaged 47,371 and held the largest total attendance in baseball in 2023; Freddie Freeman praised the four-deck stadium and its 50,000 nightly fans.
Citizens Bank Park (opened 2004) is ranked No. 1; the Phillies swept the Marlins to improve to 24-11 in postseason games there.
Two of the three postseason no-hitters in history happened at Citizens Bank Park, including Roy Halladay's in Game 1 of the 2010 NLDS against the Reds.
Bryson Stott's Wednesday grand slam drew a crowd roar so loud he said he couldn't hear himself yell at the dugout.
